title: Quantum Resources in Disorder-Free Localization Dynamics of Gauge Theories
authors: Devendra Singh Bhakuni, Giovanni Cataldi, Jad C. Halimeh, Emanuele Tirrito
abstract: Quantum-state complexity diagnostics provide valuable insight into many-body dynamics, information scrambling, and quantum computation. Here, we investigate the real-time dynamics of quantum complexity in $1+1$-dimensional Abelian U(1) and non-Abelian SU(2) lattice gauge theories (LGTs), focusing on the disorder-free localization (DFL) regime. Using stabilizer Rényi entropy, participation Rényi entropy, and fermionic non-Gaussianity as measures of complexity, we observe, for both theories, two main behaviors as a function of the gauge coupling: at intermediate values, a power-law relaxation towards saturation, consistent with observations in many-body localization, and, at sufficiently large values, an ultraslow double-logarithmic growth, which we substantiate with a configuration-space bound verified by exact counting. Our results not only provide deeper insight into the dynamics of DFL but also highlight the role of gauge invariance in constraining quantum resources and are relevant to recent quantum simulations of LGTs.
summary: This paper analyzes the real-time evolution of quantum complexity resources in 1+1D Lattice Gauge Theories under disorder-free localization. By tracking metrics like Rényi entropies, the authors characterize two distinct dynamic regimes based on the gauge coupling strength: MBL-like power-law saturation and ultraslow double-logarithmic growth. The findings highlight how fundamental symmetries constrain quantum information spreading in these strongly correlated systems.
main_problem: The study investigates how quantum resources spread in lattice gauge theories (LGTs) operating in a disorder-free localization (DFL) regime, focusing on the real-time dynamics of quantum complexity.
main_result: The research finds two distinct behaviors depending on the gauge coupling: power-law relaxation consistent with Many-Body Localization at intermediate couplings, and ultraslow double-logarithmic growth at large couplings.
method: The authors employ multiple quantum resource monotones—Stabilizer Rényi Entropy, Participation Rényi Entropy, and Fermionic Non-Gaussianity—to diagnose complexity dynamics over long time scales.
model_or_system: The models are 1+1 dimensional Abelian U(1) and non-Abelian SU(2) Lattice Gauge Theories (LGTs), formulated using Kogut-Susskind staggered fermions on a lattice chain. The analysis tracks the evolution governed by gauge constraints.
key_observables: Stabilizer Rényi Entropy ($	ext{SRE}_2$), Participation Rényi Entropy ($	ext{PE}_2$), and Fermionic Non-Gaussianity ($	ext{NG}$)
important_parameters: Gauge coupling strength ($g^2$), Time ($t$, up to $10^{15}$), Lattice size ($L$)
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that gauge invariance constrains quantum resource growth, and later sections use exact counting methods to distinguish polynomial vs. exponential scaling of resonant volumes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate LGT ingredients and show schematic summaries of resource dynamics versus $g^2$, displaying power-law saturation at intermediate couplings and double-logarithmic behavior at large couplings for U(1) LGTs.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem by defining quantum complexity diagnostics in LGTs. It then analyzes the time evolution using specific resource monotones across different coupling regimes, culminating in rigorous mathematical bounds derived from exact counting of resonant configurations to confirm the double-logarithmic growth rate.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses localization phenomena (MBL) within a complex physical framework (gauge theories), providing quantitative measures of how fundamental symmetries constrain quantum information flow, which is highly relevant for understanding dynamics in strongly interacting many-body systems.
